modules.name: Employee
modules.responsibility: Core employee lifecycle management: hire, update, transfer, promote, terminate, rehire. Manages employee master data, personal information, org chart, and headcount.
source_folders: schema/tables/01_core_tables.sql (EMPLOYEES, DEPARTMENTS, JOB_TITLES, JOB_GRADES, LOCATIONS, EMPLOYEE_HISTORY, EMPLOYEE_DEPENDENTS, EMERGENCY_CONTACTS)

evidence.reason: Dedicated package with clear public API for all employee lifecycle operations
3 DB triggers enforce employee invariants at DB level
EMPLOYEES table is the central entity; all employee data grouped in this schema file
Dedicated Oracle Form for employee management

open_questions: Are there any stored procedures for batch employee imports that are not captured in the package?
EMPLOYEE_DEPENDENTS and EMERGENCY_CONTACTS have no corresponding PL/SQL package — who manages their DML?

modules.name: Leave
modules.responsibility: Leave request lifecycle: submission, approval, rejection, cancellation. Leave balance accrual, carryover, expiry. Team calendar and pending approvals view. Monthly accrual batch job.

evidence.reason: Dedicated package with complete leave lifecycle API
Dedicated schema file for all leave-related tables
Dedicated Oracle Form for leave management

open_questions: Is there a self-service web portal (mentioned in PKG_LEAVE.pks header) that is separate from the Forms application?
Is DBMS_SCHEDULER job for run_monthly_accrual defined somewhere not in the source set?

modules.name: Payroll
modules.responsibility: Salary record management, pay period creation, payroll run lifecycle (create/calculate/approve/reverse), per-employee pay calculation, tax calculations (federal/state/FICA/Medicare), pay slip generation, pay register CSV output.
source_folders: schema/tables/02_payroll_tables.sql (SALARY_RECORDS, PAY_ELEMENTS, EMPLOYEE_PAY_ELEMENTS, PAY_PERIODS, PAYROLL_RUNS, PAYROLL_DETAILS, TAX_BRACKETS, EMPLOYEE_TAX_INFO, EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS)
entry_points: HRMS_PAYROLL form (OPEN_FORM from HRMS_MENU, requires PAYROLL VIEW permission)

evidence.reason: Dedicated package with complete payroll lifecycle API
Dedicated schema file for all payroll tables
Dedicated Oracle Form for payroll processing

open_questions: Circular dependency: PKG_EMPLOYEE calls PKG_PAYROLL.create_salary_record; PKG_PAYROLL calls PKG_EMPLOYEE.is_active. Who resolves?
TAX_BRACKETS table is defined but PKG_PAYROLL hard-codes 2024 brackets — is TAX_BRACKETS ever populated and used?

EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS table exists (for direct deposit) but no PKG_PAYROLL procedure reads or uses it — is bank account managed by a separate package outside the source set, or is direct deposit handled by an external batch/vendor process entirely?
ACH disbursement: what produces the NACHA file or bank API call after payroll approval? No code in the source performs this step.
PRENOTE_SENT / PRENOTE_DATE columns on EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS exist but are never set by any package — who owns the prenote workflow?
ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC: what routine encrypts/decrypts bank account numbers? No such function appears in PKG_SECURITY or PKG_PAYROLL.
Are DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs for payroll runs defined in a file not in scope?

modules.name: Performance
modules.responsibility: Performance review cycle management, review creation and lifecycle (self-assessment, manager review, acknowledgment), goal tracking, rating distribution, calibration support.
entry_points: HRMS_PERFORMANCE form (OPEN_FORM from HRMS_MENU, no permission check)
PKG_PERFORMANCE.generate_reviews_for_cycle (batch — creates reviews for all active employees)

evidence.reason: Dedicated package with complete performance review API
Dedicated performance tables in schema
Dedicated Oracle Form

open_questions: PKG_PERFORMANCE.pks header mentions 'batch calibration job' — where is this defined?
Rating calibration fields (CALIBRATED_RATING, CALIBRATION_NOTES) exist in table but no PKG_PERFORMANCE procedure handles calibration — is there a separate calibration package?

modules.name: Reporting
modules.responsibility: HR analytics and compliance reporting: headcount, compensation summary, turnover, new hires, leave utilization, payroll summary, EEO compliance.
source_folders: schema/views/hrms_views.sql (VW_ACTIVE_EMPLOYEES, VW_ORG_HIERARCHY, VW_EMPLOYEE_COMPENSATION, VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY, VW_PAYROLL_LATEST, VW_PENDING_APPROVALS)
entry_points: HRMS_REPORTS form (OPEN_FORM from HRMS_MENU — form not in source set)
Oracle Reports .rdf (mentioned in PKG_REPORTING.pks header — not in source)

evidence.reason: Dedicated reporting package; all procedures return REF CURSORs for use by reports/forms
6 read-only views for reporting

open_questions: HRMS_REPORTS.fmb referenced in menu but not in source set — does it exist?
RPT_* denormalized reporting tables mentioned in refresh_reporting_tables but none defined in schema — were they omitted from source?
Oracle Reports .rdf files mentioned in header — where are they?

modules.name: Integration
modules.responsibility: External system integration: GL journal feed to Oracle Financials (flat file), ADP benefits enrollment export (fixed-width file), time-and-attendance import (CSV), org structure sync (LDAP stub).
main_components: UTL_FILE (Oracle directory objects: GL_FEED_OUT, BENEFITS_FEED_OUT, TIME_ATTENDANCE_IN)

evidence.reason: 3 UTL_FILE-based integrations; FTP credentials in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS (cleartext)
Known issues: no retry logic, ADP vendor-specific format, flat file exchange

open_questions: Are the Oracle directory objects (GL_FEED_OUT, BENEFITS_FEED_OUT, TIME_ATTENDANCE_IN, PAYROLL_OUTPUT) defined in a DBA script not included in source?
import_time_attendance has TODO: parsing not implemented — is there a separate utility that does this?
sync_org_structure is a stub — is LDAP/AD sync handled by a different team/system?
FTP credentials stored in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS table — which parameters and who populates them?

modules.name: Notification
modules.responsibility: Asynchronous notification queuing and delivery via SMTP. Queues email notifications for leave approvals, employee events, performance review milestones. Batch queue processor runs every 5 minutes via DBMS_SCHEDULER.
entry_points: PKG_NOTIFICATION.send_notification (called by PKG_EMPLOYEE, PKG_LEAVE, PKG_PAYROLL, PKG_PERFORMANCE)

evidence.reason: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION ensures notification never blocks business transactions; queue-based async delivery
Known issues: no rate limiting, SMTP hard-coded to smtp.internal.company.com:25

open_questions: Is there a DBMS_SCHEDULER job definition for process_queue (every 5 minutes) in a script not in scope?
SMS and IN_APP notification types are listed in NOTIFICATION_QUEUE but process_queue only handles EMAIL — are those implemented elsewhere?

modules.name: Audit
modules.responsibility: Cross-cutting audit trail. Records all DML operations to AUDIT_LOG with old/new values, user, IP, session. Provides change history retrieval. Supports 365-day default retention with purge capability.
entry_points: PKG_AUDIT.log_action (called by all packages and DB triggers)

evidence.reason: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION; all packages call log_action; failures silently swallowed

modules.name: Security
modules.responsibility: Authentication (username/password login, session creation), session validation (30-minute timeout), grade-based authorization (has_permission), SSN encryption/decryption (AES-256), password hashing (MD5), password change.
entry_points: PKG_SECURITY.has_permission (called at form open and button press)
used_by_modules: All forms (HRMS_LOGIN, HRMS_MENU, HRMS_EMPLOYEE, HRMS_PAYROLL, HRMS_LEAVE, HRMS_PERFORMANCE)

evidence.reason: Hard-coded encryption key; MD5 password hashing; no account lockout; password verification stub
Login form; known cleartext password transmission

open_questions: USER_CREDENTIALS table referenced in PKG_SECURITY (change_password, authenticate comments) but not defined in schema — where is it?
Password verification in authenticate() appears to not verify the actual password hash — is authentication truly implemented?
Hard-coded encryption key 'HR$ystem_3ncrypt10n_K3y_2024!!' in PKG_SECURITY.pkb — is this production key?

modules.name: Validation
modules.responsibility: Reusable validation functions: date ranges, salary-grade compliance, email/phone format, employee number format, business day calculation, required field checks. Used by both server-side packages and Oracle Forms client-side.
entry_points: PKG_VALIDATION functions (called by PKG_EMPLOYEE, PKG_PAYROLL from server side)
HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB functions (called from form WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM triggers)

evidence.reason: 8 validation functions; delegates email/phone to PKG_COMMON
Client-side library with documented drift from server-side (email subdomain handling, SSN zero-segment check)

open_questions: Known drift between HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB.validate_email and PKG_COMMON.is_valid_email — which is authoritative?
validate_required_fields only handles 'EMPLOYEES' table case — is it used for other tables?

modules.name: Common
modules.responsibility: Cross-cutting utilities: error/info logging (to AUDIT_LOG), system parameter management (read/write SYSTEM_PARAMETERS), date utilities (business days, fiscal year/quarter), formatting (phone, SSN, currency, name), base validation (email, phone, SSN).
entry_points: PKG_COMMON.log_error / log_info (called from all packages on exception)
HRMS_COMMON_LIB toolbar functions (attached to all forms)

evidence.reason: No cross-package dependencies; base package called by all others
Attached to all HRMS forms; provides toolbar/session/format utilities

open_questions: LOOKUP_VALUES table has no dedicated PL/SQL package — is it read directly by forms via LOVs or does PKG_COMMON provide a get_lookup function?
Fiscal year starts October 1 per PKG_COMMON.get_fiscal_year — is this configurable via SYSTEM_PARAMETERS or always hard-coded?
